question: At what locus and in what manner should the air be drawn or drunk as prescribed?
premises: The locus is the root of the tongue and palate.
Having placed the air there, one acts.
One should drink the air slowly.
inference: At the root of the tongue and palate, having made the air [rest there], one should drink it slowly.
uncertainties: The exact technical sense of pibec in this breath practice is not determined by the verse alone.
plain_english: Having made the air at the root of the tongue and palate, one should drink it slowly.
